messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiating for model-service v5.0.0 -> prod (canary=15%). weight_manifest: weights-v5-2026-03-15, tokenizer: tok-v5-2026-03-15.json :rocket:

alex: noticing weird token splits in canary traffic. example input: `O'Connor` -> output tokens: `O'` and `Connor` separated with space. also apostrophes in contractions getting spaced. affecting entity linker.

tara: oncall here. are the failures correlated to a specific shard/host?

alex: yes. only nodes in pool model-canary-3..6. error rate on tokenization endpoint up to 22% for those nodes. other metrics (latency, throughput) look normal.

incident-bot: Paging @tara and @sre-lead — severity: SEV2. Tokenization anomalies impacting downstream NER and customer messages.

sre-lead: acknowledged. alex, capture the loaded tokenizer metadata and the loaded weight bundle from one of the failing nodes. paste the loaded manifest.

alex: failing node dump:
```
NODE: model-canary-4
LOADED_WEIGHT_MANIFEST: weights-v4-legacy-2025-12-01.manifest
REQUESTED_WEIGHT_MANIFEST: weights-v5-2026-03-15.manifest
TOKENIZER_ID: tok-v5-2026-03-15.json
TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM: 3b7d9c11
RUNTIME_ENV: WEIGHT_SET=${WEIGHT_SET}
```

alex: interestingly the requested weight manifest is correct but the loaded manifest is v4-legacy. looks like runtime resolved to a fallback weightset for some nodes. tokenizer checksum matches v5, but tokenizer behavior looks like it was loaded from a v4-style tokenizer (legacy splitting rules).

tara: could be a mapping bug where legacy shard mapping is applied when the new weightset has fewer shards and the deploy agent falls back. check the mapping table: `shard_map.json` on node.

alex: shard_map on node shows `map_version: 13` and an override `shard_alias: legacy->weights-v4-legacy` present. that alias was recently added by a hotfix in infra last month.

pm-voice: summarizing customer impact: inbound/outbound messages with names containing punctuation are mangled for customers on multi-tenant plans routed to canary. we've got an open ticket C-9981, two paying customers reporting deliverability/appearance issues.

sre-lead: immediate mitigation: pause the rollout and route new canary traffic to stable pool. then force a restart of affected nodes to ensure they load correct manifests.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause received. Current rollout halted at 15% traffic.

tara: doing a quick experiment: set runtime flag `weights-fallback-disabled=true` to prevent the agent fallback. That should force the node to fail fast instead of silently using legacy weights. I'll flip and watch.

alex: command run:
```
$ infractl featureflag set weights-fallback-disabled --env prod --value true --scope canary
# applied to nodes model-canary-3..6
```

incident-bot: Feature flag update detected: `weights-fallback-disabled = true` by tara. Notifying watchers.

alex: after flag, nodes started returning 503 for model load errors (expected). we then triggered a rolling restart which forced them to pick the requested artifact. new logs show load path `artifact://weights-v5-2026-03-15/*` and tokenizer behaviors reverted to expected (no apostrophe splits). error rates dropped to baseline.

customer-ops: informed customers that we've paused rollout and applied mitigation. asked for hand-validated samples; one customer confirmed improved appearance on new messages, historical queued messages still show corruption. they want reprocessing for the last 90 minutes.

sre-lead: ok. plan: 1) keep rollout paused, 2) revert any infra alias `legacy->weights` that causes silent remapping, 3) add preflight assertion in deploy pipeline that the node loaded the requested manifest and tokenizer checksum matches before letting it join traffic, 4) trigger reprocess job for impacted tenants.

alex: I opened infra ticket INFRA-4823 to remove the alias and added a short-lived rollback to ensure nodes request consistent manifests. also added a local validation script:
```
# check loaded vs requested
python tools/check_manifest.py --node model-canary-4 --expect weights-v5-2026-03-15.manifest
# exit non-zero if mismatch
```

tara: also adding a canary test in release pipeline: feed canonical punctuation-sensitive prompts and assert tokenization matches golden outputs. will add as gate.

incident-bot: Handoff: @tara (oncall) handing to @sre-lead for active remediation. Severity downgraded to SEV3 as we paused rollout and immediate customer-facing errors reduced.

sre-lead: taking ownership. leaving notes: root cause appears to be silent remapping fallback to legacy weights due to infra alias. short-term fix: disable fallback + restart nodes. Long-term: remove alias and add manifest-check gate. Follow-ups assigned: INFRA-4823, DEPLOY-5234 (canary tokenization test), OPS-7301 (reprocess queue).

customer-ops: customers acknowledged the mitigation steps; reprocess requested and scheduled. will follow up in ticket C-9981.

pm-voice: added postmortem owners and scheduled blameless review for tomorrow. action items: remove alias, add manifest checksum in deployment agent, integrate tokenizer canonical tests in CI, and evaluate adding alerting for manifest mismatch rate.

sre-lead: noted. leaving thread open for progress updates and verification. :white_check_mark:
